newsitem.title: CANADA: Hudson's Bay sees more improvement in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Hudson's Bay sees more improvement in 1997.

text.p: Hudson's Bay Co said on Thursday it expects its financial results to continue improving into 1997 as consumer spending increases and the retailer's restructuring efforts begin to pay off.

"The increase in consumer spending in the fourth quarter of 1996 is expected to continue in 1997 and this, along with internal initiatives, should allow the company to continue to generate improved results," HBC said in a statement after releasing fourth-quarter and 1996 earnings.
The retailer, Canada's oldest, owns the Zellers and The Bay chains, with over 400 stores across Canada.
HBC's earnings per share increased 98 percent in the fourth quarter to C$1.36 from C$0.70 a year earlier.

Restructuring costs of C$64 million earlier in the year pulled down the full-year results. For the year ending January 31 earnings per share edged up to C$0.61 from C$0.59. Before restructuring, earnings were C$1.22 per share.
The company said it was encouraged by the improved second half results and anticipated seeing continued benefits from the restructuring.
"The benefits of consolidating the Zellers operational offices with the Bay's offices and HBC corporate started to show in the fourth quarter and will accelerate in 1997," HBC said.
